```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
# Run once in the R console if needed:
# install.packages(c("foreign", "knitr", "rmarkdown"))
default_params <- list(
  "data-file" = "Case 31 Data_efcu_1_cleaned.sav",
  "repo-url" = "",
  "pages-url" = ""
)
if (!exists("params", inherits = FALSE) || !is.list(params)) params <- list()
for (key in names(default_params)) {
  if (is.null(params[[key]])) params[[key]] <- default_params[[key]]
}
for (pkg in c("foreign", "knitr")) {
  if (!requireNamespace(pkg, quietly = TRUE)) {
    stop(paste("Install the required package first:", pkg))
  }
}
candidate_paths <- c(params[["data-file"]],
                     file.path("data", params[["data-file"]]),
                     file.path("case31", params[["data-file"]]))
candidate_paths <- candidate_paths[file.exists(candidate_paths)]
if (!length(candidate_paths)) {
  stop("Place Case 31 Data_efcu_1_cleaned.sav beside this QMD, or update params:data-file.")
}
raw <- foreign::read.spss(candidate_paths[1], to.data.frame = TRUE,
                          use.value.labels = FALSE, use.missings = TRUE)
names(raw) <- tolower(names(raw))
dat <- raw
keep_codes <- function(x, valid) {
  x <- as.numeric(x)
  x[!is.na(x) & !(x %in% valid)] <- NA_real_
  x
}
required <- c("q7", "q8", "q9", "q10", "q11", "q12",
              paste0("q", 13:26), paste0("q", 30:34), "q37")
stopifnot(all(required %in% names(dat)))
# Recompute from ORIGINAL variables; never reverse an existing reversed item.
dat$q7r <- 6 - keep_codes(raw$q7, 1:5)
dat$q8r <- 6 - keep_codes(raw$q8, 1:5)
dat$q9r <- 6 - keep_codes(raw$q9, 1:5)
dat$q10r <- 5 - keep_codes(raw$q10, 1:4)
dat$q11 <- keep_codes(raw$q11, 1:2)
dat$q12rc <- keep_codes(raw$q12, 1:2)
dat$q37r <- 6 - keep_codes(raw$q37, 1:5)
for (v in paste0("q", 30:34)) dat[[v]] <- keep_codes(raw[[v]], 1:5)
awareness_vars <- paste0("q", 13:26, "r")
for (i in 13:26) dat[[paste0("q", i, "r")]] <- 4 - keep_codes(raw[[paste0("q", i)]], 1:3)
N <- nrow(dat)
service_names <- c("Regular share accounts", "Special subaccounts",
                   "Christmas club accounts", "Individual retirement accounts",
                   "MasterCard credit cards", "Signature loans", "New car loans",
                   "Late-model car loans", "Older-model car loans",
                   "Household goods/appliance loans", "Recreational loans",
                   "Share-collateralized loans", "IRA loans", "Line-of-credit loans")
fmt <- function(x, digits = 2) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits)
p_fmt <- function(p) ifelse(p < .001, "< .001", sub("^0", "", fmt(p, 3)))
p_statement <- function(p) ifelse(p < .001, "p < .001", paste0("p = ", p_fmt(p)))
pct <- function(x, digits = 1) paste0(fmt(100 * x, digits), "%")
count_pct <- function(n, total) paste0(n, " (", pct(n / total), ")")
share <- function(v, codes) mean(dat[[v]][!is.na(dat[[v]])] %in% codes)
freq <- function(x, labels) {
  counts <- as.integer(table(factor(x, levels = seq_along(labels))))
  data.frame(Response = labels, n = counts,
             "Valid %" = pct(counts / sum(counts)), check.names = FALSE)
}
one_sample <- function(vars, labels, mu = 3) {
  out <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(vars), function(i) {
    x <- dat[[vars[i]]]
    x <- x[!is.na(x)]
    result <- t.test(x, mu = mu, alternative = "two.sided", conf.level = .95)
    data.frame(Item = labels[i], Variable = vars[i], n = length(x),
               Mean = mean(x), SD = sd(x), Median = median(x),
               CI_low = result$conf.int[1], CI_high = result$conf.int[2],
               t = unname(result$statistic), df = unname(result$parameter),
               p = result$p.value, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }))
  out$p_holm <- p.adjust(out$p, method = "holm")
  out
}
describe_table <- function(tests) {
  data.frame(Item = tests$Item, n = tests$n, Mean = fmt(tests$Mean),
             SD = fmt(tests$SD), Median = fmt(tests$Median, 1),
             "95% CI for mean" = paste0(fmt(tests$CI_low), "–", fmt(tests$CI_high)),
             check.names = FALSE)
}
test_table <- function(tests) {
  data.frame(Item = tests$Item, "Mean − 3" = fmt(tests$Mean - 3),
             t = fmt(tests$t), df = tests$df, p = p_fmt(tests$p),
             "Holm p" = p_fmt(tests$p_holm), check.names = FALSE)
}
equal_gof <- function(x, k) {
  counts <- as.integer(table(factor(x, levels = seq_len(k))))
  # Include zero-count categories in the specified null distribution.
  test <- chisq.test(counts, p = rep(1 / k, k))
  data.frame(n = sum(counts), X2 = unname(test$statistic),
             df = unname(test$parameter), p = test$p.value,
             min_expected = min(test$expected))
}
show_table <- function(x) {
  knitr::kable(x, format = "html", escape = TRUE,
               row.names = FALSE, table.attr = 'class="analysis-table"')
}
r1 <- one_sample("q7r", "Savings-rate perception")
r2 <- one_sample(c("q8r", "q30"), c("Q8r Borrowing-rate perception", "Q30 CU rates lower than competitors"))
awareness <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(awareness_vars), function(i) {
  x <- dat[[awareness_vars[i]]]
  counts <- as.integer(table(factor(x, levels = 1:3)))
  data.frame(Variable = awareness_vars[i], Service = service_names[i],
             n = sum(counts), Unaware = counts[1],
             Aware_not_used = counts[2], Used = counts[3],
             Aware = counts[2] + counts[3])
}))
awareness_gof <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(awareness_vars), function(i) {
  cbind(Service = service_names[i], equal_gof(dat[[awareness_vars[i]]], 3))
}))
awareness_gof$p_holm <- p.adjust(awareness_gof$p, "holm")
awareness_table <- data.frame(
  Item = paste0("Q", 13:26), Service = awareness$Service,
  "Used n (%)" = count_pct(awareness$Used, awareness$n),
  "Aware, not used n (%)" = count_pct(awareness$Aware_not_used, awareness$n),
  "Unaware n (%)" = count_pct(awareness$Unaware, awareness$n),
  "Total aware" = pct(awareness$Aware / awareness$n), check.names = FALSE)
categorical_vars <- c("q9r", "q10r", "q11", "q12rc")
categorical_names <- c("Q9 Statement frequency", "Q10 Statement accuracy",
                       "Q11 Easy to understand", "Q12 Account confidentiality")
categorical_k <- c(5, 4, 2, 2)
categorical_gof <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(categorical_vars), function(i) {
  cbind(Item = categorical_names[i], equal_gof(dat[[categorical_vars[i]]], categorical_k[i]))
}))
categorical_gof$p_holm <- p.adjust(categorical_gof$p, "holm")
operations <- one_sample(c(paste0("q", 31:34), "q37r"),
                         c("Q31 Financial information confidential", "Q32 Prompt loan processing",
                           "Q33 Services meet needs", "Q34 Simple loan applications",
                           "Q37r Overall management and operations"))
options(digits = 4, width = 100)
```

## Purpose and sample

EFCU wants to understand low borrowing and members' views of its services and operations.
This report analyzes **R1, R2, R5, and R6** using the cleaned Module 10 dataset.

- **`r N` responses** are available. Percentages use each item's valid responses.
- The case used a mail survey and a simple random sample of 300 from a membership frame of 3,531.
- Q2 and Q28–Q29 are absent from this dataset. Rate perceptions provide context for R1 and R2, but cannot establish members' actual reasons.

::: {.note}
The narrative describes 125 returns and 123 usable questionnaires; the supplied teaching dataset contains `r N` rows. The analysis uses the supplied data. A response rate is not calculated from these inconsistent counts.
:::

## Analysis plan

| Research question | Available measures | Analysis |
|---|---|---|
| **R1** Reasons for joining | Q7r Savings-rate perception | Frequencies and one-sample t-test |
| **R2** Reasons for outside borrowing | Q8r Borrowing-rate perception; Q30 Comparative rates | Frequencies and one-sample t-tests |
| **R5** Service awareness | Q13r–Q26r | Frequencies and chi-square goodness-of-fit tests |
| **R6** Operational effectiveness | Q9r–Q10r, Q11–Q12rc, Q31–Q34, Q37r | Frequencies, chi-square goodness-of-fit tests, and one-sample t-tests |

::: {.note}
Tests follow the instructor's worked example. The t-test benchmark is 3. Goodness-of-fit tests use equal proportions across all valid response categories. Two-sided tests use α = .05; Holm adjustments are reported within related sets of tests.
:::

## R1 Why do people join the Credit Union?

**Descriptive statistics · Savings-rate perceptions (Q7r)**

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
```{r}
#| label: tbl-r1-frequency
#| tbl-cap: "Q7r Savings-rate perceptions"
#| results: asis
show_table(freq(dat$q7r, c("Very low", "Low", "Average", "High", "Very high")))
```
:::
::: {.column width="52%"}
As @tbl-r1-frequency shows, **`r pct(share("q7r", 3))`** of valid respondents rate savings rates as average; **`r pct(share("q7r", 4:5))`** rate them high or very high.

There are `r r1$n` valid responses and `r N - r1$n` excluded responses.

The results do not show a clear perception of unusually high savings rates. Q2 is needed to determine whether rates actually motivated joining.
:::
::::

## R1 One-sample t-test

Compare the mean savings-rate rating with **3 = average**.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r1-descriptive
#| tbl-cap: "Q7r Descriptive statistics"
#| results: asis
show_table(describe_table(r1))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r1-test
#| tbl-cap: "Q7r Two-sided one-sample t-test against 3"
#| results: asis
show_table(test_table(r1)[, c("Item", "Mean − 3", "t", "df", "p")])
```

::: {.takeaway}
The average rating is **`r fmt(r1$Mean)`**, close to the scale's average category. The test provides insufficient evidence of a difference from 3 (t(`r r1$df`) = `r fmt(r1$t)`, `r p_statement(r1$p)`; @tbl-r1-test). This does not prove that the population mean equals 3.
:::

**Descriptive statistics · Two views of EFCU's loan rates**

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
```{r}
#| label: tbl-r2-rate-frequency

show_table(freq(dat$q8r, c("Very low", "Low", "Average", "High", "Very high")))
```
::: {.note}
Valid n = `r r2$n[1]`; `r N - r2$n[1]` excluded. Higher scores mean higher rates.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="52%"}
```{r}
#| label: tbl-r2-comparison-frequency
#| tbl-cap: "Q30 CU rates are lower than competitors'"
#| results: asis
show_table(freq(dat$q30, c("Strongly disagree", "Disagree", "Uncertain", "Agree", "Strongly agree")))
```

:::
:::
::::

::: {.compact}
Most valid Q8r responses are **average (`r pct(share("q8r", 3))`)**. For Q30, **`r pct(share("q30", 3))` are uncertain** and `r pct(share("q30", 4:5))` agree that CU rates are lower (@tbl-r2-rate-frequency; @tbl-r2-comparison-frequency).
:::

## R2 One-sample t-tests

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r2-descriptive
#| tbl-cap: "Loan-rate perceptions Descriptive statistics"
#| results: asis
show_table(describe_table(r2))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r2-tests
#| tbl-cap: "Loan-rate perceptions Two-sided t-tests against 3"
#| results: asis
show_table(test_table(r2))
```

::: {.compact}
Neither mean differs significantly from 3 at .05 (@tbl-r2-tests). There is no clear evidence here that members see a strong rate advantage.

**Actual outside-borrowing reasons remain unanswered.** Q28 identifies outside borrowers and Q29 asks why they borrowed elsewhere; both are missing. These ratings alone cannot show that price caused borrowing decisions.
:::

## R5 How well are members aware of services?

```{r}
#| label: fig-r5-awareness
#| fig-cap: "Awareness and use by service; the right column shows total awareness"
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 4.6
#| fig-dpi: 170
#| out-width: "100%"
ord <- rev(order(awareness$Aware / awareness$n))
plot_data <- t(as.matrix(awareness[ord, c("Used", "Aware_not_used", "Unaware")]))
plot_data <- sweep(plot_data, 2, awareness$n[ord], "/") * 100
par(mar = c(2.8, 14.6, 3.2, 4.6), family = "sans", col.axis = "#17324d",
    fg = "#17324d", cex = .93)
bar_y <- barplot(plot_data, horiz = TRUE, border = NA, xlim = c(0, 100),
                 names.arg = awareness$Service[ord], las = 1,
                 col = c("#147d85", "#a4d5d4", "#e4e9ee"),
                 xlab = "", axes = FALSE, space = .32)
axis(1, at = seq(0, 100, 20), labels = paste0(seq(0, 100, 20), "%"), tick = FALSE)
legend("top", inset = c(0, -.08), xpd = NA, horiz = TRUE, bty = "n",
        legend = c("Aware and used", "Aware, not used", "Unaware"),
        fill = c("#147d85", "#a4d5d4", "#e4e9ee"), cex = .86)
text(103, bar_y, pct(awareness$Aware[ord] / awareness$n[ord]),
     pos = 4, xpd = NA, cex = .87, col = "#17324d")
```

::: {.note}
Total aware = aware and used + aware but not used. Each service has `r min(awareness$n)` valid responses. See @tbl-r5-frequency-a and @tbl-r5-frequency-b for counts.
:::

## R5 Descriptive statistics Q13–Q19

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r5-frequency-a
#| tbl-cap: "Service awareness and use Q13–Q19"
#| results: asis
show_table(awareness_table[1:7, ])
```

::: {.compact}
**Regular share accounts have the lowest awareness (`r pct(awareness$Aware[1] / awareness$n[1])`).** Confirm that members understand this product name before treating this result solely as a communication problem.
:::

::: {.note}
Percentages use valid responses within each service. “Used” means aware and have used; it does not measure current holdings or recent activity.
:::

## R5 Descriptive statistics Q20–Q26

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r5-frequency-b
#| tbl-cap: "Service awareness and use Q20–Q26"
#| results: asis
show_table(awareness_table[8:14, ])
```

::: {.compact}
**Line-of-credit loans are universally recognized in this sample**, but only `r pct(awareness$Used[14] / awareness$n[14])` report ever using them. Awareness and use describe different parts of the borrowing opportunity.
:::

## R5 Chi-square goodness-of-fit tests {.dense}

For each service, H₀ specifies **one-third in each awareness/use category**; Hₐ specifies at least one different proportion.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r5-tests
#| tbl-cap: "Awareness distributions compared with equal thirds"
#| results: asis
show_table(data.frame(Service = awareness_gof$Service,
                      "χ²" = fmt(awareness_gof$X2), df = awareness_gof$df,
                      p = p_fmt(awareness_gof$p),
                      "Holm p" = p_fmt(awareness_gof$p_holm), check.names = FALSE))
```

::: {.note}
All three categories remain in every test, including Q26's zero “unaware” responses. Minimum expected count = `r fmt(min(awareness_gof$min_expected), 1)`. Equal thirds is the instructor's comparison distribution, not an EFCU performance target.
:::

## R5 What the results mean

- **Awareness varies substantially.** It ranges from `r pct(min(awareness$Aware / awareness$n))` for regular share accounts to `r pct(max(awareness$Aware / awareness$n))` for line-of-credit loans (@fig-r5-awareness).
- **Some recognized loans have limited use.** Signature loans are known by `r pct(awareness$Aware[6] / awareness$n[6])`, yet `r pct(awareness$Used[6] / awareness$n[6])` have used them. New car loans show a similar gap (@tbl-r5-frequency-a).
- **All 14 distributions differ from equal thirds**, including after Holm adjustment (@tbl-r5-tests). The direction comes from the frequencies: unawareness is not the largest category for every service.

::: {.takeaway}
Use targeted explanations for poorly recognized products and investigate barriers for well-known loans with low use. The survey does not establish which action will increase borrowing.
:::

**Descriptive statistics · Statement frequency and accuracy**

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r}
#| label: tbl-r6-frequency
#| tbl-cap: "Q9 Statement frequency"

show_table(freq(dat$q9r, c("Never", "Not often enough", "About right", "Very often", "Too often")))
```
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r}
#| label: tbl-r6-accuracy

#| results: asis
show_table(freq(dat$q10r, c("Poor", "Fair", "Good", "Excellent")))
```
:::
::::

Most members say statement frequency is **about right (`r pct(share("q9r", 3))`)**, but **`r pct(share("q9r", 2))` want statements more often** (@tbl-r6-frequency). Statement accuracy is rated good or excellent by `r pct(share("q10r", 3:4))` (@tbl-r6-accuracy).
:::

## R6 Understandability and confidentiality

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r6-binary
#| tbl-cap: "Yes/no operational responses"
#| results: asis
binary_vars <- c("q11", "q12rc")
show_table(do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(binary_vars), function(i) {
  x <- dat[[binary_vars[i]]]
  n_valid <- sum(!is.na(x))
  data.frame(Item = c("Q11 Statements easy to understand", "Q12 Account information confidential")[i],
             "Valid n" = n_valid, "Yes n (%)" = count_pct(sum(x == 1, na.rm = TRUE), n_valid),
             "No n (%)" = count_pct(sum(x == 2, na.rm = TRUE), n_valid),
             Excluded = N - n_valid, check.names = FALSE)
})))
```

Statements are understandable to **`r pct(share("q11", 1))`** of respondents.

Confidentiality deserves follow-up: **`r sum(dat$q12rc == 2, na.rm = TRUE)` of `r sum(!is.na(dat$q12rc))` valid respondents (`r pct(share("q12rc", 2))`) answer no**, while `r sum(is.na(dat$q12rc))` responses are excluded (@tbl-r6-binary).

::: {.note}
Q12's code 3 means no answer and is excluded. It is not a third substantive opinion. Q31 separately asks about personal financial information, so the two items should not be treated as identical.
:::

## R6 Chi-square goodness-of-fit tests

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r6-categorical-tests
#| tbl-cap: "Categorical operational responses compared with equal category proportions"
#| results: asis
show_table(data.frame(Item = categorical_gof$Item, n = categorical_gof$n,
                      "χ²" = fmt(categorical_gof$X2), df = categorical_gof$df,
                      p = p_fmt(categorical_gof$p),
                      "Holm p" = p_fmt(categorical_gof$p_holm), check.names = FALSE))
```

All four distributions differ from equal category proportions, including after Holm adjustment (@tbl-r6-categorical-tests).

The frequencies show where responses concentrate: **about-right frequency, good/excellent accuracy, and yes on understandability and confidentiality**.

::: {.note}
H₀ uses 20% per Q9 category, 25% per Q10 category, and 50% yes/50% no for Q11 and Q12. Hₐ specifies at least one different proportion. These are classroom reference distributions; rejecting them does not by itself establish acceptable performance. All expected counts exceed 5.
:::

## R6 Operational ratings Descriptive statistics

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r6-ratings
#| tbl-cap: "Operational ratings on their respective five-point scales"
#| results: asis
rating_table <- describe_table(operations)
rating_table$Median <- NULL
rating_table[["Favorable %"]] <- vapply(operations$Variable, function(v) pct(share(v, 4:5)), character(1))
show_table(rating_table)
```

::: {.compact}
Overall management is rated good/excellent by **`r pct(share("q37r", 4:5))`** of valid respondents. Among Q31–Q34, confidentiality has the highest mean and simple loan applications the lowest (@tbl-r6-ratings).
:::

::: {.note}
Q31–Q34: 1 = strongly disagree, 3 = uncertain, 5 = strongly agree; favorable = agree/strongly agree. Q37r: 1 = very poor, 3 = average, 5 = excellent; favorable = good/excellent. Q37 excludes `r N - operations$n[5]` responses.
:::

## R6 One-sample t-tests

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r6-rating-tests
#| tbl-cap: "Operational ratings Two-sided one-sample t-tests against 3"
#| results: asis
show_table(test_table(operations))
```

::: {.takeaway}
All five mean ratings exceed their midpoint, with sufficient evidence of differences after Holm adjustment (all adjusted p < .001; @tbl-r6-rating-tests). Members generally evaluate operations positively.
:::

::: {.compact}
The positive overall assessment still leaves room to improve application simplicity and address the statement-frequency and confidentiality concerns shown in @tbl-r6-frequency and @tbl-r6-binary.
:::

## Recommended next steps

1. **Check product understanding.** Verify the unusually low recognition of regular share accounts, then clarify names and benefits for poorly recognized services.
2. **Investigate the gap between awareness and use.** Ask members who know about signature and car loans what prevents use before choosing a campaign or pricing change.
3. **Follow up on operational concerns.** Explore statement-frequency preferences, the Q12 confidentiality concerns, and friction in loan applications.
4. **Collect the missing decision evidence.** Obtain Q2, Q28, and Q29 to answer the joining and outside-borrowing questions directly.

::: {.note}
These are recommendations based on the response patterns, not tested causal effects. Self-reported use is not an observed borrowing or conversion rate.
:::

## Appendix Data coding and exclusions {.dense}

| Variables | Coding used in this report | Exclusions |
|---|---|---|
| Q7r, Q8r | 6 − original Q7/Q8; 1 = very low, 5 = very high | Original code 6 and missing values |
| Q13r–Q26r | 4 − original Q13–Q26; 1 = unaware, 2 = aware/not used, 3 = aware/used | Missing or invalid responses |
| Q9r | 6 − original Q9; 1 = never, 5 = too often | Missing or invalid responses |
| Q10r | 5 − original Q10; 1 = poor, 4 = excellent | Missing or invalid responses |
| Q11, Q12rc | 1 = yes, 2 = no | Code 3 = no answer |
| Q30–Q34 | Original agreement scores; 1–5 | Missing or invalid responses |
| Q37r | 6 − original Q37; 1 = very poor, 5 = excellent | Original code 6 and missing values |

::: {.note}
All recodes are derived from original columns. Q9r measures frequency, not a uniformly favorable scale: “about right” is the desired response. Items with different meanings and scales are analyzed separately.
:::

## Appendix Valid responses and assumptions

```{r}
#| label: tbl-missingness
#| tbl-cap: "Items with excluded responses"
#| results: asis
show_table(data.frame(Item = c("Q7 Savings rates", "Q8 Borrowing rates",
                               "Q12 Confidentiality", "Q37 Overall management"),
                      "Valid n" = c(sum(!is.na(dat$q7r)), sum(!is.na(dat$q8r)),
                                    sum(!is.na(dat$q12rc)), sum(!is.na(dat$q37r))),
                      Excluded = c(sum(is.na(dat$q7r)), sum(is.na(dat$q8r)),
                                   sum(is.na(dat$q12rc)), sum(is.na(dat$q37r))),
                      check.names = FALSE))
```

::: {.compact}
- All other reported items have `r N` valid responses. Missing responses are excluded item by item; no values are imputed.
- T-tests follow the class's interval approximation for numerical rating scores. Goodness-of-fit tests retain zero-count categories and have adequate expected counts.
- Responses are treated as independent across members. Separate service tests are adjusted together using Holm's method; R2's two tests and each R6 test family are adjusted separately.
- The findings describe the supplied respondents. Nonresponse and the mismatch with the narrative's sample count limit population generalization.
:::
